title: Six Winters and One Short Letter
subtitle: 情感心理 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事）
meta: 主题语境：情感心理（人与自我·做人与做事）　|　核心词汇：envy　|　正文 341 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 envy 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1948 my aunt ① felt an envy that no neighbour in the yard would have named, and she said the feeling was the whole of the winter. The ② envy, meaning the feeling itself and not the praise, ran six winters and stayed unnamed in the book; an envy, she said, is the only thing in a yard that is judged by how long it is left unnamed.

Every ③ envy in that yard had the same short letter beside it, and the ④ envy at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the sister and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An envy, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to name; my aunt said the naming is the part that fills six winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the envy was the whole of the wish, meaning the object and not the feeling. The ⑥ envy, meaning the object and not any of that, is the only thing in a wish that everybody wants and nobody names; envy, he said, is either something you feel or the only word that means both a feeling and an object. He said the object is the part they remember.

By 1954 the ⑦ envy had become a line in a diary, and the diary had become an argument about the short letter. The ⑧ envy of the whole thing, my aunt wrote in January, was one yard and six winters of naming; envy, she said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to name. She said the naming was never mentioned.

The ⑨ envy I remember is the one named in the diary, which closed in 1957 and is still described as the quietest in the yard. An ⑩ envy, my mother said in 1959, is the only one that improves by being named; every envy, she said, is an object that has agreed to look like a feeling. She said the object was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 羡慕；嫉妒（指院子里每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 羡慕（指那一份本身，与赞赏相对）
C. 固定搭配：feel an envy 感到羡慕
D. n. 羡慕（指留给妹妹的那一份）

F. n. 羡慕（指日记上写到、被记下的那一份）
G. n. 羡慕的对象（指人人都想拥有却无人承认的那样东西）
H. n. 羡慕（抽象总称，指人人都想拥有却无人承认的那种心情）

answers.why: feel an envy 意为“感到羡慕”，1948 年姑姑感到了一份院子里没有一位邻居肯命名的羡慕。
envy 意为“羡慕”，指那一份本身而不是赞赏，它经过了六个冬天而在簿子上没有名字。
envy 意为“羡慕”，指院子里每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一封短短的信。
envy 意为“羡慕”，指留给妹妹的那一份，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
envy 意为“羡慕的对象”，指人人都想拥有却无人承认的那样东西，叔叔说这个对象就是那个心愿的全部。
envy 意为“羡慕”，指人人都想拥有却无人承认的那种心情而不是那一份感情，是心愿里人人都想要、却无人命名的东西。
envy 意为“羡慕”，指日记上写到、被记下的那一份，到 1954 年这一份成了日记里的一行。
envy 意为“羡慕”，姑姑一月写道，整件事的羡慕之事是一个院子和六个冬天的命名。
envy 意为“羡慕”，我记得的是日记上记下的那一份，1957 年结束了，至今仍被说成院子里最安静的一份。
envy 为抽象总称，母亲 1959 年说，一份羡慕是唯一会因为被好好命名而变得更好的东西。
